title: A Cursed Mask Coldly Laughs
notes: Detective-cast nodes (Conan, Kogoro Mouri, Ran, plus minor recurring police Inspector, Officer Kobayashi, Detective Takagi) omitted by convention. No `event` node type: every action is a directly typed, attributed edge between the entities involved. case_type: murder. The old wiki-summary case file (cases/ep184_...json) correctly identified the culprit (Toya Aikawa) and the broad backstory (Beniko caused the hit-and-run that killed Katagiri's wife, then murdered Toya's mother and staged it as suicide to cover it up), so `label.murderer_id` is unchanged from the old file. However the old file mislocated the murder itself 'in the mask room' -- the transcript is explicit that the mask room (l1) is only where the 200 Jofre masks and knife were normally displayed and stolen from; the actual stabbing happened through a barred transom into Beniko's separate third-floor bedroom (l2), fired remotely from the sealed, vacant adjoining bedroom (l3) via a private east-wing-only staircase (l4) -- that geography IS the locked-room trick and was entirely missing from the old file. The old file also omitted: the extension-phone taunting call Aikawa used to build a false alibi, Kogoro's red-herring accusation of secretary Kazuyo Inaba (no motive ever established for her), the twin maids and baseball-player/tarot-reader suspects, Beniko's alleged charity-fund embezzlement (an unverified accusation made only by the culprit during his confession, not confirmed independently), and the precise physical/testimonial clues (bloodied knife handle, mask blood-distribution pattern, Aikawa's slip about Ran/Conan's movements, the no-footprints-in-snow deduction).

objects.name: Chain of the 200 masks of Jofre (murder instrument)

attrs.provenance: carved by Spanish sculptor Jofre Gonzales, said to be cursed to 'sip the blood' of their owners; normally displayed in the mask room (l1), owned by Beniko Suou
attrs.trick: all 200 masks (each 15mm thick) threaded eye-to-eye on a rubber rope, with the rope also passed through a hole in the knife's pommel, to form one rigid, extendable 3-meter rod that could be pushed and pulled from the adjoining room
attrs.blood_distribution: only the topmost/final mask nearest the wound was heavily blood-soaked; the rest show blood only around the mouth-hole where the rope was threaded -- proof of the chain mechanism rather than a supernatural attack

attrs.provenance: normally displayed in the mask room (l1), owned by Beniko Suou
attrs.anomaly: found with its handle smeared in blood despite never having been gripped by a hand -- it was propelled on the far end of the mask chain via the rubber rope threaded through its pommel
attrs.reach: the final ~10cm of blade closed the gap once the 3-meter mask chain had crossed the 3.5m from transom to bed

attrs.trick: threaded through both eyeholes of every mask and through the knife's pommel hole to lock the masks and knife into a single rigid rod; severed and withdrawn by the killer after the killing so no rope was left in the sealed bedroom

Aikawa used it to call Mouri's east-wing guest room with a taunting 'the cursed masks thirst for blood' message just before the murder, to make it appear he was confined to the east wing at the moment of death

clues.desc: Aikawa let slip that he knew Ran and Conan had gone to wake Honami together, via a story about cracking his door open to look -- but in fact Conan had split off from Ran to go check the mansion's other doors for locks. Aikawa could only have assumed they were together by having actually watched the third-floor corridor near Beniko's room at the time of the murder, which the east-wing staircase (l4) made possible.

No footprints were found in the fresh snow outside the mansion, and the doors connecting the east and west wings were confirmed locked at the time of death -- seemingly proving the killer had to be physically confined among the five guests then in the west wing. This premise only held until the private east-wing staircase to the third floor (l4), bypassing the wings' lock entirely, was uncovered, which is what actually let an east-wing occupant commit the murder.
